reach.text: Free school meals and the bus cap are for England. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

sources.note: Annex B.13, comparability factors at Spending Review 2025

pitch.text: Energy bills are rising again this winter. People need to feel this Budget in their pockets before Christmas, not read about it in a forecast.

reaction.text: Good. That is the one thing people will feel before Christmas. I will want to know what pays for it.
reaction.short: Good. People will feel that before Christmas. What pays for it?

priorities.title: Bring down NHS waiting lists
priorities.purpose: England’s 18-week waiting promise, and social care.

reach.text: Health and care budgets here are England’s. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

sources.note: Annex B.13, comparability factors at Spending Review 2025

pitch.text: The waiting list is falling and the 18-week target is within reach. And I have promised a national care service without yet finding the money for it.

reaction.text: Eighteen weeks is the promise people remember. Protect it.

priorities.title: Defence on the NATO path
priorities.purpose: Fund the defence plan. Aim for 3% of national income.

pitch.text: The defence of our nation will always be my first priority. The Defence Investment Plan is published and £4.7 billion of it is waiting for you.

reaction.text: That is not a favour to the Defence Secretary. It is a commitment we have published.
reaction.short: Not a favour to the Defence Secretary: a commitment we have published.

reach.text: Schools and skills budgets here are England’s. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

pitch.text: Special needs deficits are about to hit council reserves. Councils are about to hit the wall on this, and the plans keep rising.

reaction.text: Councils are about to hit the wall on this. Yes, and quickly.

priorities.title: Homes and growth outside London
priorities.purpose: Build homes and invest, visibly, outside London.

reach.text: Council homes here are England’s. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

sources.note: Annex B.13, comparability factors at Spending Review 2025

pitch.text: This will be a Budget that moves money and power out of Westminster. Council homes are the fair way to bring the welfare bill down. Show the country that re-industrialising Britain is real.

reaction.text: Power and money out of Westminster. That is the whole point of us.
reaction.short: Power and money out of Westminster: the whole point of us.

pitch.text: Ending the two-child limit lifted 450,000 children out of poverty. I want this Budget to go further for families, not back.

reaction.text: Families first. The party will like that a great deal, and so will I.
reaction.short: Families first. The party will like that, and so will I.

priorities.title: Safer streets: prisons, police, borders
priorities.purpose: Prison places for the sentences promised.

reach.text: Prisons, courts and police here are England and Wales’s. Scotland and Northern Ireland get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

pitch.text: I have told the House that the worst offenders will serve their full terms, and that needs prison places. Bring the asylum bill down and the whole department breathes.

priorities.title: Get the welfare bill down
priorities.purpose: A smaller benefits bill, with savings that are real.

pitch.text: Council homes are the fair way to bring the welfare bill down. If you want to go faster than that, be honest about who loses.

reaction.text: Careful. The last reform missed its savings, and the party will read every line.
reaction.short: Careful. The last reform missed its savings; the party reads every line.

promises.title: The tax lock
promises.text: We will not increase National Insurance, the basic, higher, or additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT. The manifesto's words, repeated at Budget 2025.

sources.quote: Labour will not increase taxes on working people, which is why we will not increase National Insurance, the basic, higher, or additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT.

strains.text: A levy on pay and employers is National Insurance by another name.
Employer National Insurance is not named in the pledge; it is still National Insurance.
Employer National Insurance is not named in the pledge; it is still National Insurance.
Employer National Insurance on pensions: not named in the pledge, still National Insurance.
An employer-style National Insurance charge on partners: not named in the pledge, still National Insurance.
A new top rate is not a rise in the three named rates, and it is an income tax rise.

promises.title: Corporation tax capped at 25%
promises.text: We will cap corporation tax at the current level of 25 per cent, the lowest in the G7, for the entire parliament.

sources.quote: Labour will cap corporation tax at the current level of 25 per cent, the lowest in the G7, for the entire parliament.

promises.title: The two-child limit stays abolished
promises.noun: the promise on the two-child limit
promises.text: Ending the two-child limit from April 2026 lifts 450,000 children out of poverty. A Budget 2025 decision, not a manifesto promise: bringing the limit back is a U-turn.

sources.quote: We are lifting 450,000 children out of poverty with the end of the two-child limit.

promises.title: The fiscal rules
promises.text: We will abide by the fiscal rules, ensuring we retain a buffer to protect us against uncertainty. The Chancellor's own words to the Treasury Committee.

sources.quote: we will abide by the fiscal rules, ensuring we retain a buffer to protect us against uncertainty and the impact of instability in the Middle East

promises.title: Defence on its path
promises.text: The manifesto set the path to 2.5% of GDP; the government has since committed to 3% in the next Parliament and 3.5% by 2035. A cut to day-to-day defence slows that path.

sources.quote: the UK has committed to reach 3.5% of GDP on defence spending by 2035

strains.text: A cut slows the path to 3.5% of GDP by 2035.

promises.title: The triple lock
promises.text: Labour will retain the triple lock for the state pension: it rises each year by the highest of earnings growth, prices or 2.5%. The OBR's forecast assumes it.

sources.quote: Labour will retain the triple lock for the state pension.

strains.text: Mostly the state pension. A cut keeps the lock’s words only if it falls on pension credit or winter fuel.

promises.title: NHS waits within 18 weeks
promises.text: Patients should expect to wait no longer than 18 weeks from referral for consultant-led treatment: the manifesto's words, for the NHS in England. The plan is 9 in 10 within 18 weeks by the end of the Parliament.

sources.quote: patients should expect to wait no longer than 18 weeks from referral for consultant-led treatment

strains.text: A cut to the health budget puts the 18-week target at risk.
